findings.title: The journey that claims to run the 2-second limit sets NIO_PERF for the wrong command
quotes: NIO_PERF=1 uv run python tests/test_implement.py && uv run python tests/test_flow.py && echo ok
findings.fix: change the journey command so that `NIO_PERF=1` is on `test_flow.py`: `uv run python tests/test_implement.py && NIO_PERF=1 uv run python tests/test_flow.py && echo ok`.

sources.situation: Shell inline variables apply to the first command only. `tests/test_flow.py`, the file that holds `test_nfr3_status_speed`, runs with `NIO_PERF` unset. If `nio flow status` regresses to 5 seconds, this journey still passes. The output shows "ok (3.00s)" and "ok (2.80s)" with no failure. The `NIO_PERF=1` environment is only passed to `test_implement.py`, which does not use it.

findings.reason: results.json line 242 holds the command `NIO_PERF=1 uv run python tests/test_implement.py && uv run python tests/test_flow.py && echo ok`. An inline variable applies only to the first command, so `test_flow.py` runs with `NIO_PERF` unset. That means the 2-second assert in `test_nfr3_status_speed` never fires, which is what AC-18 and AC-29 are about.
findings.note: Delegated human (orchestrator): QS-5 checks UJ-5, a review on a loaded machine with NIO_PERF=1 in the caller's env; asserting the 2-second limit there would fail under load, which US-5 removes. The limit stays the manual self-check of FR-15/FR-18. C-261106-mao2 rejected, T-15 retired.
findings.where: the `NIO_PERF=1` journey command (journeys in the evidence pack); `tests/test_flow.py:test_nfr3_status_speed`

findings.title: The status-speed assertion was weakened and nothing automated runs it
findings.fix: keep it as specified. Have a scheduled or manual gate run `NIO_PERF=1 uv run python tests/test_flow.py`. Correct the F1 journey so that at least one recorded run asserts the limit.

sources.situation: The old test always asserted `took < 2.0`. It now asserts the limit only when `NIO_PERF` is exactly "1". The review's `run` strips `NIO_PERF` by design (CT-9), and CLAUDE.md asks only for a manual run. Status speed can therefore regress unnoticed through every automated gate, and the F1 journey does not catch it either. Nothing marks this as a deliberate weakening other than the spec itself.

findings.title: The printed timing in the status-speed test is misleading
findings.fix: print the status-run time that `status_speed` measures (return it as well as the output), or drop the number from the line.

sources.situation: `start` is taken before `status_speed()`, which also builds 20 efforts with 50 history lines each. The printed value (3.00s, 2.80s in the pack output) is setup plus status. A reader comparing it with the 2-second limit would see a figure over the limit next to "ok".

findings.title: AC-14 and AC-15 tests sit after the `__main__` runner and never run
findings.fix: move the T-5 tests and the `perf_suite` helper above the `if __name__ == "__main__":` block in `tests/test_implement.py`, then re-run the suite and confirm the new tests print "ok".

sources.situation: `test_ac14_review_strips_nio_perf`, `test_ac15_review_still_fails` and `test_ac14_review_strips_nio_perf_misuse` are appended under "# --- T-5: the review strips NIO_PERF (CT-9, FR-11) ---", after the `__main__` loop. Running `python tests/test_implement.py` defines them only after the loop has finished. The passing suite and the journey runs therefore prove nothing about FR-11. The code in `src/nio/implement.py:run` could be reverted and the suite would still pass.

`uv run python tests/test_implement.py` reaches the `if __name__ == "__main__":` block at line 1662 and runs only the tests defined above it. The new `test_ac14_review_strips_nio_perf` and `test_ac15_review_still_fails` are defined at lines 1678 and 1699, after the loop has already run. The suite therefore reports `ok` for `test_implement.py` without ever checking that the review strips `NIO_PERF` (AC-14) or still fails a broken assertion (AC-15). If the review regressed, the gate would still pass.

findings.reason: In tests/test_implement.py the `__main__` runner is at lines 1662-1669, and the three T-5 tests (lines 1678, 1699, 1715) are defined after it. The loop iterates `globals()` before they exist, so they never run under `python tests/test_implement.py`. FR-11 is therefore unchecked by the suite.
findings.where: tests/test_implement.py (end of file, after the `__main__` block)

findings.title: AC-14 and AC-15 tests sit below the file's runner and never run
quotes: +# --- T-5: the review strips NIO_PERF (CT-9, FR-11) ---
findings.fix: move the `if __name__ == "__main__":` block (lines 1662-1669) to the end of `tests/test_implement.py`, after the T-5 tests, so every test is defined before the runner.
